positive: Many commenters praise the opening and closing animation as smooth, clean and polished, calling it a standout of the presentation and crediting the design team.
Several note that the inner screen appears to show no visible crease, and see the matte finish as a smart way to hide it.
Some say the animation responds to the hinge angle, suggesting app developers could build on it, and even skeptics admit it looks impressive.
negative: Several are unimpressed by the fold animation, calling it a blur effect and saying it doesn't justify the hype or the price. One notes it was quickly recreated on a Samsung foldable.
Viewers see the price as too high compared with Samsung's foldables and past Apple products. Some worry about repair costs and regional markups.

positive: Several self-described Samsung foldable users say they are surprised and impressed by how polished Apple's first foldable looks.
Some commenters credit Apple for software and app polish, and for features like MagSafe, while noting Android foldables lack fully optimized apps.
Others stay loyal to Samsung, noting its screen supply and foldable experience, while expecting Apple's entry to push competitors and the market forward.
negative: Several accuse Apple of copying Samsung or repackaging old ideas, and say Apple fans cheer for features they once dismissed.
Some note Samsung supplies Apple's screens, and a few predict the device will be short-lived or has quality drawbacks.

positive: Many viewers were pleasantly surprised by the iPhone Duo, praising its design, matte inner screen, minimal crease and polished unfolding animation, and some now consider buying it.
Several commenters prefer the Samsung Fold 8's look, citing its thin, light, symmetrical, rectangular shape, and some say they are watching on one.
Some believe Apple's ecosystem, durability and unfolded aspect ratio could give the Duo an edge over other foldables, and Fold users welcome Apple to the category.
negative: Commenters say Apple is arriving years after Samsung and Google in foldables, yet its fans and marketing treat the idea as new.
Many criticise the high price, saying it costs as much as an iPhone plus an iPad, and that Samsung offers better value.
The outer screen's shape, aspect ratio and rounded corners are called odd or impractical, and some prefer Samsung's front screen and desktop-style features.

positive: Many commenters expected a higher launch price and were pleasantly surprised it came in around $2,000.
Several see the price as in line with other foldables, especially Samsung's, and consider that reasonable or competitive.
Some welcome the added competition in foldables and say the price helps make the category more appealing.
negative: Many commenters see the foldable's price as extremely high, with some saying it effectively costs as much as two phones.
Regional pricing draws particular criticism: viewers in India, Mexico and Europe say it is out of reach for most local incomes.
Several say they can't afford or justify a phone this expensive, and compare it unfavorably with cheaper foldables from other brands.

positive: Many commenters prefer a clean inner screen with no cutout or dot, and are happy to trade some selfie quality for it.
Several say they rarely use the inner camera, since selfies usually come from the outer display or the main cameras, and they mostly watch and scroll.
negative: Many point out that under-display cameras already existed on other phones, so they see it as no real innovation from Apple.
Commenters say image quality suffers under the screen, and many would prefer a visible punch-hole for better selfies.
The camera is still noticeable on the display, so it isn't truly hidden and looks unappealing to several viewers.

positive: Many left-handed commenters say they are used to right-handed designs, often hold their phone in the right hand anyway, and see the layout as a non-issue.
Several see the right-side dock and control placement as a sensible design choice rather than a flaw, and right-handed users who favour their left hand are also unbothered.
negative: Many commenters say the design and interface favor right-handed one-handed use, making the phone awkward or nearly unusable for left-handed people.
Hardware features like the fingerprint sensor, outer display, cameras and dock sit on one side, so software fixes alone wouldn't fully help.

positive: Apple Pencil compatibility came as a pleasant surprise and was a deciding factor for several viewers, including some who plan to pre-order or switch from Android foldables.
Android foldable owners say Apple's pen support beats their own device, which lacks stylus support, and they hope Samsung brings its pen back.
Commenters see pen support as a boost to productivity, letting the inner screen work like a mini iPad alongside premium features such as water resistance.
negative: Many commenters say the foldable's lack of Apple Pencil support makes it less useful for drawing or note-taking, even though the price is high.
Several worry that a hard pencil tip could scratch or damage the folding inner screen, and question its durability.
Some compare it with Samsung's S Pen and say Apple is copying rivals or removing features instead of innovating.

positive: Many commenters praise the smooth fold and unfold transition, often describing the outer screen as see-through glass revealing the inner display.
The nano-texture inner display is welcomed for its matte look, reduced fingerprints, and for hiding reflections that would show the fold crease.
Some see the matte surface as a good match for Apple Pencil support, similar to paper-feel screen protectors on iPads.
negative: The change from the glossy outer display to the matte inner one looks odd, and the coating is seen as a trade-off for a crease that was already barely noticeable.
Commenters worry about the inner screen's durability, since a screen protector can't be used and leaving it open risks scratches.

positive: Many commenters are excited and ready to preorder or buy the Duo as soon as it launches, some with little hesitation.
Some long-time iPhone owners say the new design finally gives them a reason to upgrade, calling it fresh, different and appealing.
Others like the look and practical benefits, such as replacing both phone and tablet, and say the price with a trade-in seems reasonable.
negative: Many are interested but see the price as too high, and say they can't justify it or will stay with their current phone.
Several plan to wait for a later generation, expecting lower prices, fewer first-version flaws and less weight.
Some see better value in a Pro Max or an iPad mini, citing the cameras, Face ID, and the foldable's weight.

positive: Several viewers like Apple's folio case for the Duo, saying it looks good and keeps the front screen free of touches, smudges and scratches.
Some say the case and accessory support, such as MagSafe and Pencil, push them toward buying the Duo, though price puts others off.
negative: Folio and kickstand cases are seen as awkward: covering the front or camera makes photos and quick payments harder, and there is no outer view window.
Commenters worry the phone is already heavy, thick and bulky, and a case adds more weight and size.
Some question whether cases protect the exposed outer screen and edges, or fix wobble when the device is open.

positive: Many commenters expect a well-known durability YouTuber to put the phone through bend and stress tests, and joke that it may not survive.
Some think Apple designed it with that kind of testing in mind, for example by reinforcing weak points like the antenna line, and are confident it will hold up.
Reactions are mixed: some are excited and want to buy it, while others wait for long-term durability results or compare it with rival foldables.
negative: Commenters worry the foldable's durability is unproven, especially given the high price, and want independent testing before buying.
Many expect the screen to show a crease along the fold within months, and to scratch easily under scratch tests.
Some think the design looks fragile, fearing a single drop could break it or that antenna line placement weakens the structure.

positive: Many commenters are choosing between a dark blue-black (Night Sky) and white, with plenty already decided on one or the other.
Night Sky is praised as understated and attractive, though one person prefers white because the dark finish makes the bezels look larger.
Some plan to buy larger storage tiers, and a few pair their color with a taupe folio case or want to see the colors in person first.
negative: Many commenters worry about battery life and are frustrated that Apple gives unclear battery figures, confusing runtime claims and an unhelpful battery indicator.
Storage-tier pricing is seen as very high in Australia and New Zealand, particularly for the larger capacities, though some say they will still buy.
Some dislike the color choices and naming, finding them hard to read as plain white or black, and note inaccurate color on the inner display.

positive: Commenters are excited that Apple is trying something new, and some say it is their most interesting iPhone in years.
Several praise the software for the form factor, including smooth transitions, side toolbar, and navigation that works in any orientation, along with a useful folio design.
negative: Many see the foldable design as unoriginal, pointing to existing foldables from Samsung, RedMagic and Microsoft's Surface Duo, with Apple only now catching up.
Several worry about size and practicality: it seems too big for pockets or comfortable one-handed use, and may be awkward for left-handed users.
Others criticise design choices and durability: a covered or unusable front screen, return of fingerprint unlock over Face ID, fragile folding screens, and a high price.

positive: Several say the software, including the animations and new ways of using the folding screen, impresses them even if they are unsure about foldables.
Some note rivals offer more features and flexibility, but Apple's ecosystem and app support are expected to set the Duo apart.
negative: Many commenters say Apple's foldable and its software features feel derivative, since Samsung, Microsoft and others already offered similar hardware and multitasking ideas.
Some doubt the software is a real advantage: Apple took years to arrive at similar hardware, and app support from developers may lag.
A few argue software experience can make or break a foldable, with some preferring Apple's control of both hardware and software.

positive: Many commenters are enthusiastic and plan to buy or pre-order the Duo, including long-time Apple users and some Android users who express admiration.
The software is praised, especially the fold transition animations, with some saying Android makers should focus more on UI and polish, not just hardware.
Weight and thickness against Samsung's foldable come up, as does the premium build, along with jokes about Samsung supplying the displays.
negative: Many see the Duo name as a weak or confusing choice, with jokes that it points to double pricing or echoes the Microsoft Surface Duo.
Commenters mock Apple for treating small tweaks, like a less visible crease or later design changes, as big innovations, and for relying on Samsung parts.
Some complain the phone is heavy, thick, expensive and awkwardly shaped, and say the folded look bothers people who prefer symmetry.

positive: Several commenters dismiss durability worries, noting the shown device was just a plastic dummy and the real phone uses a sturdier metal build.
Many say the high price is normal for foldables and reflects the two screens, so lacking pro-level features is not a flaw.
Viewers are excited about the opening animation and Apple's ecosystem, saying it finally makes a folding phone appealing and could replace a phone-plus-tablet setup.
negative: Many commenters expect the hinge and crease to wear out over time, and doubt the foldable will hold up to long-term use.
Several worry the exposed inner screen is hard to protect, that cases are limited, and that one drop could destroy it.
Commenters question whether such a high price is justified for a fragile device, especially when other brands have offered folding phones for years.

positive: Many viewers praise the design and attention to detail, especially the smooth opening animation and the way the interface suits the foldable screen.
Commenters see practical value in the format, such as reading documents or charts on the go, and like the vertical orientation and camera bump placement.
Some are enthusiastic but cautious, saying they might wait for later generations or compare it with Samsung foldables they already enjoy.
negative: Several raise practical drawbacks: a visible crease, hinge durability, camera compromises, no Face ID, awkward size and folio use, and a matte finish that hurts video contrast.
Some are sarcastic about Apple's foldable being first or novel, noting that Android makers and Microsoft's earlier Duo got there first, while still praising the video.

positive: Many commenters see the foldable as a way to replace carrying a tablet, getting a bigger screen in a pocketable device.
Work and accessibility uses come up often: reading plans or manuals, larger text, and more usable space for older eyes.
Several like the wider shape and bigger display for video, gaming, multitasking and reading, and some expect better app support.
negative: Many see the Duo as essentially a small iPad in phone form, arriving years after rivals, with little real innovation beyond polish.
The matte inner screen draws criticism for looking dull and washed out, especially in sunlight, and for losing glossy colour saturation.
Software and practicality concerns: limited multitasking (such as no two apps in landscape), cramped home layout, scarce developer support, awkward cases, and very high price and repair costs.

positive: Many praise iOS as refined, polished and simple, saying its redesign for the foldable is what makes the device appealing, more than the hardware alone.
Several say Apple's entry shifted their view: people previously uninterested in foldables, including some Android fans, now find it impressive or tempting.
Commenters value thoughtful details such as better multitasking, app layouts that fit the wider screen without changes, and a movable dock for left-handed users.
negative: Many commenters say the price is too high, and that it is far worse outside the US once taxes and local pricing are added.
Several feel the reviewers downplayed the fold crease and the opening mechanism, and see the device as unpolished or overly staged.
Android users say foldables already offer these features, that iOS multitasking and app optimisation lag behind, and that few would switch.

positive: Commenters praise the hinge as properly engineered, contrasting it with hollow mockups and suggesting it is durable and not a copy of other foldables.
Many like the rounded, booklet-like edges and the flat side, saying they feel soft, pocket-friendly, easier to hold and look good opened.
Several doubt the device breaks easily and favor a sturdier build, while the glass-style opening animation and interface also get strong praise.
negative: Commenters doubt that an IP68 rating means much on a foldable, since the hinge area stays exposed and dust can get in.
Some expect the hinge to wear out or fail with frequent opening and closing, and say water and dust resistance will fade over time.
People say they would not take a very expensive foldable to the beach unprotected, and note that rival foldables with similar ratings still had problems.

positive: Many commenters are eager to buy the foldable, with some planning to preorder or get it soon after launch, and a few waiting until next year.
Some prefer to wait for a second generation or compare rivals first, treating this as an impressive first attempt that signals better versions ahead.
Viewers like the design details, camera setup and durability confidence, and some mention trade-in deals or timing around their current phone upgrade.
negative: Many commenters say foldable phones are not new, accusing Apple of arriving years late and copying other brands while being praised as innovative.
Commenters expect Apple to hold back features such as a telephoto camera, a smaller bezel or a better screen, then add them next year at a higher price.
The high price, basic cameras and design drawbacks like the closed shape and large bezel lead some to wait for a later model.

positive: Several commenters like the Duo's design but wish it came with the Pro-level cameras, since camera quality is the one thing they feel is missing.
Others argue it isn't a Pro model, so lacking Pro cameras isn't a real sacrifice. Some say moving down from a Pro felt fine.
Many are interested but cautious, preferring to wait for later versions or keep their current Pro phone, partly because of the high price.
negative: Many commenters say the Duo's cameras fall short of the Pro's, such as the missing telephoto and main lens, and that this is a dealbreaker at its price.
The price is widely seen as too high, especially in countries like India, Canada and Australia, and some predict weak sales.
Other missing features also put people off: no Face ID, a matte display, weaker battery, extra weight, poor speakers and no quick action button.

positive: Several commenters welcome the return of Touch ID and see the lack of Face ID as a reason to buy, not a drawback.
Fingerprint unlocking is described as fast and more convenient than face unlock, especially at a desk or when entering a PIN often.
Watch unlock support and Pencil compatibility are cited as features that won over people who were doubtful about the device.
negative: Some find a fingerprint sensor inconvenient, citing accessibility problems such as difficulty using their fingers, and worry about smudges.

positive: Many commenters repeat a wordplay about Steve, Tim and John as successive Apple leaders, suggesting the new leader's era is now beginning.
The folding animation draws praise as smooth and polished, with a see-through look and a level of detail seen as typical of Apple.
Some viewers say they plan to buy the device despite criticism, and others joke that it suits watching a film in its intended format.
negative: Many commenters say Apple has lost its innovative spark since Steve Jobs died, and that current products and keynotes feel uninteresting by comparison.
Several imply Jobs would have disapproved of this device, suggesting it would have been rejected or the team punished.

elements.text: Example of the Slack digest, to show the format. Figures are illustrative and not guaranteed to be accurate. Ask a follow-up: mention the app or message it. The full report is in your inbox.

examples.q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
examples.a:
Small channels break out most: 36% of the 89 small-channel videos with a baseline were outperformers (110 videos total), compared with 22% for mid (n=50 with baseline) and 5.3% for large (n=38). Average relative lift follows the same order: about 8.0x for small, 3.7x for mid, and 1.3x for large.

Audience sentiment is mixed and fairly close across groups. Net sentiment on product-side comments is +0.06 for small (n=2,717 comments), +0.11 for mid (n=2,354), and -0.03 for large (n=1,965). Mid-size audiences are the happiest, with 41.7% positive against 30.8% negative. Large-channel audiences lean slightly negative (38.8% negative vs 36.2% positive).

Caveat: these are associations from a comment sample, and the large and mid groups have fairly few videos with a baseline, so the outperformer rates are less stable than the comment counts suggest.
examples.sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), perf AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM v GROUP BY size_group), sent AS (SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_raw FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.size_group) SELECT perf.size_group, perf.n_videos, perf.n_with_baseline, perf.outperformer_rate, perf.avg_rel_lift, sent.n_product_side, sent.pct_positive, sent.pct_negative, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN sent.net_raw END AS net_sentiment FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent ON sent.size_group=perf.size_group ORDER BY perf.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
examples.a:
First impressions is the only format with a usable sample: 8 of 19 videos (42%, 16 channels) outperformed, with an average relative lift of 2.7. Full review and durability test both show a 100% outperformer rate, but each is a single video (n=1), so that's an anecdote, not a pattern.

Explainer/tips is mixed (n=8): only 12.5% outperformed, yet its average relative lift is high at 9.7, which suggests one or two big hits are pulling the average up. Comparison (n=6), upgrade advice (n=8), meme shorts (n=3), keynote recaps (n=2) and other (n=2) had no outperformers.

Caveat: these are associations in a small mid-tier sample, not proof that a format causes the lift, and most formats have too few videos to rank confidently.
examples.sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(DISTINCT c.channel_id) AS n_channels, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.lift),3) AS avg_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' AND p.outperformer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
examples.a:
Two clear examples: "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" (Time Travel Visuals) and "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" (TechDroider).

The Camera Disappears short has the most negative reaction: net sentiment -0.60 (70% negative, 10% positive, n=77 product-side comments). Its lift is huge, at 499x with 20.5M views (rel_lift 72.9).

The TechDroider hands-on is next: net sentiment -0.52 (70% negative, 18% positive, n=56), with 87x lift on 1.97M views (rel_lift 12.7).

Both have reasonable comment counts, so the sentiment reads are fairly solid. Third place is a Digit Hindi comparison at -0.46, but with only n=24.

Caveat: these are comment samples and show association only. High lift and negative sentiment appearing together doesn't mean the negativity drove the views.
examples.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS channel, cr.tier, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, s.n_product_side DESC LIMIT 10

examples.q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
examples.a:
Samsung Did It First is the largest topic (n=822, 8.2% of comments), followed by Eager to Buy (n=571, 5.7%), Praise for review quality (n=543, 5.4%) and Price Complaints (n=479, 4.8%).

The fastest riser is Left-Handed Concerns. It went from 13 comments (1.4% share) to 89 (3.3%), a gain of 2.0 points. Waiting for Next Year is next, from 10 to 51 comments (1.0% to 1.9%). Apple Software Integration (8 to 35) and the reviewer speaking-style criticism topic (4 to 22) also grew, but from small bases. No Face ID grew the most in relative terms (1 to 14), but that n is too small to read much into.

Total comments rose from 954 to 2,666, so most topics grew in raw count. Share change is the better guide. Samsung Did It First lost a little share (-0.7 points) despite its raw growth.

These figures come from a comment sample, so they show associations, not causes.
examples.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM base), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS t_all, SUM(d>m-7) AS t_this, SUM(d<=m-7 AND d>m-14) AS t_prev FROM base, mx), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(d>m-7) AS n_this, SUM(d<=m-7 AND d>m-14) AS n_prev FROM base, mx WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/tot.t_all,3) AS share_all, a.n_this, a.n_prev, ROUND(1.0*a.n_this/NULLIF(tot.t_this,0),3) AS share_this_week, ROUND(1.0*a.n_prev/NULLIF(tot.t_prev,0),3) AS share_prev_week, ROUND(1.0*a.n_this/NULLIF(tot.t_this,0)-1.0*a.n_prev/NULLIF(tot.t_prev,0),3) AS share_change, ROUND(1.0*(a.n_this-a.n_prev)/NULLIF(a.n_prev,0),3) AS count_growth, tot.t_this AS all_this_week, tot.t_prev AS all_prev_week FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: How does audience sentiment on the iPhone Duo compare with the iPhone 18 Pro?
examples.a:
The iPhone 18 Pro gets somewhat better net sentiment than the Duo, though the two are close on positivity. Across all product-side comments, the 18 Pro nets +0.122 (n=3,452, 112 videos) versus +0.053 for the Duo (n=7,036, 190 videos). Positive share is nearly identical (39.1% vs 39.3%), but the Duo draws more negativity (33.9% vs 26.9%).

By target:
- Product itself: 18 Pro +0.191 (n=2,814) vs Duo +0.142 (n=4,909).
- Competitor comments: 18 Pro +0.433 (n=231) vs Duo +0.337 (n=826).
- Apple brand: both negative, the 18 Pro far more so (-0.647, n=156) than the Duo (-0.326, n=567).
- Price/value: both negative, with the Duo worse (-0.565, n=734) than the 18 Pro (-0.462, n=251).

Caveat: the 18 Pro's per-target samples are small (n=156 to 251), so those gaps are less reliable. This reflects a comment sample, not causes.
examples.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic, m.target, m.sentiment, m.video_id FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND c.format!='official' AND c.topic IN ('duo','iphone_18_pro')), allrows AS (SELECT topic, 'all product-side' AS target, sentiment, video_id FROM base UNION ALL SELECT topic, target, sentiment, video_id FROM base) SELECT topic, target, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive')-AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM allrows GROUP BY topic, target ORDER BY target, topic LIMIT 40

examples.q: What do people like most about the Duo, and what do they criticise most?
examples.a:
The clearest positive is purchase excitement. "Eager to Buy" had 256 positive vs 127 negative comments (n=571), with people wanting to pre-order or upgrade. The Samsung Fold comparison topic (n=448) is 47% positive, but its description suggests many of those commenters are praising Samsung, so I wouldn't read it as love for the Duo. The crease and fold animation is also fairly positive, though split (123 positive, 109 negative, n=271).

The biggest criticisms are price (197 negative, n=479, about 41%), durability doubts about folding phones (179 negative, n=455), and the claim that Apple copied Samsung or came late (324 negative, n=822, but 322 positive, so it's split). The under-display camera skews most negative (125 negative vs 72 positive, n=301).

Caveat: topics overlap and sentiment is often mixed, so treat these as associations in a comment sample.
examples.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND cm.topic_id IS NOT NULL), agg AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(c.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(c.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='positive')/COUNT(*),3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='negative')/COUNT(*),3) AS neg_share FROM c JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id GROUP BY t.topic_id) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, name, summary, n_product_side, n_pos, n_neg, pos_share, neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, summary, n_product_side, n_pos, n_neg, pos_share, neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8)
